^Femur
The thigh bone, the longest and strongest bone; hip joint above, knee below.
Carries body weight and the pull of the hip and thigh muscles through every stride.
Femoral (neck or shaft) stress fractures with sudden increases in training.
^Patella
The kneecap, a bone inside the quadriceps tendon; it gives the quadriceps leverage.
Glides in the groove of the femur as the knee bends and straightens.
Kneecap (patellofemoral) pain from poor tracking or weak hips and quads.
^Tibia
The shin bone, which carries most of the weight of the lower leg.
Absorbs the impact of every foot strike.
Shin splints and tibial stress fractures.
^Fibula
The thin outer bone of the lower leg; it anchors muscles and forms the outer ankle.
Steadies the ankle; carries a small share of the load.
Fibular stress fractures; fractures in ankle sprains.
^(Talus|Calcaneus|Navicular|Cuboid)
A tarsal bone of the ankle and rear foot.
Transfers body weight from the leg into the foot; the heel (calcaneus) meets the ground first in a heel strike.
Heel pain (plantar fasciitis at the calcaneus) and navicular stress fractures.
cuneiform
A wedge-shaped tarsal bone in the middle of the foot that forms the arch.
Keeps the arch stiff for push-off.
Midfoot pain or stress injury.
metatarsal
A long bone of the forefoot.
Takes the load as the foot rolls through to push-off.
Metatarsal stress fractures, especially the second and third.
toe|sesamoid
A bone of the toes.
The toes, especially the big toe, give the final push-off.
Sesamoiditis, turf toe and stress injury of the toes.
^Humerus
The upper-arm bone; shoulder joint above, elbow below.
Swings with the arms to balance the legs.
Rarely injured in running.
^(Radius|Ulna)
A forearm bone; the radius and ulna rotate around each other to turn the palm.
Part of the arm swing.
Wrist fractures when falling on an outstretched hand.
carpal|^(Capitate|Hamate|Lunate|Pisiform|Scaphoid|Trapezium|Trapezoid|Triquetrum)$
A small carpal bone of the wrist.
Keeps the wrist relaxed and steady.
Scaphoid fracture from falling on the hand.
metacarpal
A long bone of the palm.
Minor role.
Fractures from falls.
phalanx
A finger or thumb bone.
Minor role: keep the hands loose.
Finger fractures from falls.
^Clavicle
The collarbone: the only bony link between the arm and the trunk.
Steadies the shoulder during the arm swing.
Fractures from falls onto the shoulder.
^Scapula
The shoulder blade; it anchors the rotator cuff and slides on the rib cage.
Moves with the arm swing; its position sets the posture of the shoulders.
Shoulder-blade muscle tension with a hunched posture.
^(Atlas|Axis|C[3-7])
A cervical vertebra of the neck.
Holds the head balanced over the shoulders.
Neck strain with a forward head posture.
^T\d
A thoracic vertebra; the ribs attach to it.
Keeps the upper back upright and allows the trunk to rotate against the arm swing.
Upper-back stiffness with hunched running.
^L\d
A lumbar vertebra of the lower back.
Carries the upper body and absorbs impact.
Low-back pain, often from weak core or tight hip flexors.
^(Sacrum|Coccyx)
The base of the spine, wedged between the hip bones.
Transfers load from the spine to the pelvis.
Sacroiliac joint pain; sacral stress fracture.
^Hip bone
The hip bone (ilium, ischium and pubis): forms the pelvis and the hip socket.
Anchors the glutes, hip flexors and hamstrings; keeps the pelvis level.
Pelvic stress fractures and apophysis injuries in young runners.
^Rib
A rib: protects the heart and lungs and moves with breathing.
Expands with each breath; rotates slightly with the trunk.
Rarely injured in running.
^Sternum|^Costal
The breastbone and the cartilage that joins the ribs to it.
Lets the rib cage expand for breathing.
Rarely injured.
Thyroid
The thyroid cartilage of the larynx (Adam's apple).
Part of the airway.
Not a running injury site.
Mandible
The lower jaw.
A relaxed jaw reduces neck and shoulder tension.
Jaw clenching adds upper-body tension.
A bone of the skull.
Protects the brain and carries the eyes, ears and airway; the head should stay level.
Head injury from falls.
